units.arms: a list of three objects with the keys of ARM: arm 1, arm 2, arm 3
units.arm1_caption: text: one line beside arm 1's prompt number
units.arm2_caption: text: one line beside arm 2's prompt number
units.arm3_caption: text: one line beside arm 3's prompt number and on the end card
units.pp_ratio: arms[1].pp4096 / arms[0].pp4096 as the sitting reports it (paired by round); computed when absent
units.host_cols_before: arm 1: host columns a layer (token x expert pairs the CPU computes), mean over layers
units.host_cols_after: arm 2: host columns a layer, mean over layers
units.streamed_per_layer: arm 2: experts a streaming layer copies into the ring for this prompt only, mean over the layers that streamed
units.streamed_layers: arm 2: layers whose stream ran (xstream end layers); 0 leaves the ring off the stage
units.admit_per_layer: arm 2: experts a layer the pick moves into the card's seats (they stay for the decode); 0 draws no seats path
units.ring_half: arm 2: slots in one half of the ring
units.card_experts_per_layer: experts a layer the card holds before the prompt (drawing only, never printed)
units.before_label: text: arm 1's name in the stage, lanes and end card
units.after_label: text: arm 2's name in the same places
units.title: text: the title line under the version (': faster prompts' is added when pp_ratio >= 1.02)
units.answers_tag: text: after 'answers +M%' on the numbers scene and the end card, e.g. '(MTP off)'; empty adds nothing
units.conditions: text: model, card, placement, server; shown under every number (the scenes add the prompt length)
units.method_line: text: how the numbers were taken, one short line on the end card; empty hides it
units.topk: experts each token picks a layer
units.model: text: the model's name in the title
units.decode_note: text: why the answer is faster too
units.side2: text: second side line (empty string hides it)
units.source: text: where the numbers come from
units.arms[i].label: text: the arm's name on screen
units.arms[i].file: text: the model file's short name
units.arms[i].file_gb: GB = 1e9 bytes, the model file's size (du -h prints GiB, ~7 % lower)
units.arms[i].decode: tok/s, decode after the prompt_tokens prompt
